newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia YTL plans bonus, special issues.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia YTL plans bonus, special issues.

text.p: Malaysian infrastructure developer YTL Corp Bhd said on Monday it was proposing a one-for-two bonus issue, a special issue and a bond issue.
In a statement, the company said the issues were to partly fund its acquisition of shares in associate YTL Power International Sdn Bhd, which it was planning to list separately.
YTL had previously announced that it plans to hold all of its power generation interests under YTL Power International, and then list it on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
The company proposes to part finance its subscription of 700 million shares at par in YTL Power prior to the listing.
The planned bonus issue would capitalise up to 198.8 million ringgit. The issue comprises 397.6 million new shares at a par value of 50 cents, the statement said.
YTL also planned a special issue of 29.3 million new shares to approved Bumiputra (ethnic Malay) investors.
It has also proposed to issue 300 million zero coupon redeemable unsecured bonds with a maximum of 79.5 milion detachable warrants.
The offer price for the warrants will be determined at a later date.

YTL said the bonus issue will increase the number of shares to a level which will reflect the net tangible assets of the group, while the proposed special issue is intended to comply with a regulatory requirement on Bumiputra shareholding in listed companies.
The company said the bonus and special issues will add 426.9 million shares to its issued share capital of 602.3 million as at Dec 23.

Full conversion of transferable subscription rights amounting to 183.4 million and full conversion of another 9.5 million Euroconvertible bonds would raise the total existing share capital to 1.22 billion.
The proposed issues are subject to regulatory approvals, including those from the central bank, the Securities Commission and YTL shareholders.
